title: 3 things every booking page needs to convert.
styleLine: ONE CONSISTENT LINE ACROSS ALL IMAGES (critical). Cinematic editorial photography, shot as if by the SAME photographer on the SAME 35mm lens, same warm natural grade — deep navy shadows (#262B38) + warm cream light (#F7F8EA), rich but natural (NOT a heavy Instagram filter, NOT washed-out, NOT HDR). Modern boutique-hotel world: walnut wood, cream plaster, greenery, contemporary fixtures. NO dated props. Elegant, quiet, expensive. 4:5 (1080x1350). No text, no logos, no clearly identifiable faces.
note: Path B — scene/organic. The three things a booking page needs. s3 is a frameless composite — clean editorial scene with UI screenshot overlaid freely. Claims audited: the speed bar now matches the standard c13 publishes, and the parity line states what parity actually binds.

slides.headline:
3 things separating a
==booking page== from a brochure.
slides.sub: Miss any one and the guest books on Booking instead.
slides.imagePrompt: A guest smiling gently while booking on a laptop at a bright modern café or home desk (three-quarter, face not clearly identifiable), warm daylight, plant and coffee, walnut and cream. Effortless, satisfying booking moment. LEAVE THE TOP THIRD a calm brighter wall for the headline; subject lower-right. CRITICAL: any darker area must be darker ONLY because the scene's own light falls off naturally — NOT because a dark band, gradient, vignette or overlay has been applied. There must be NO horizontal boundary, step, line or abrupt change of tone anywhere in the frame; brightness must fall away gradually and continuously. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]

slides.title: ==2.5 seconds.== That's the bar.
slides.body: Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5s is what Google calls good. The average hotel page takes 6.3. On mobile that gap is the whole game.
slides.imagePrompt: A sheer white curtain lifting gently in a breeze beside a tall sunlit window in a boutique hotel room, warm morning light spilling across cream plaster and a walnut sill, a small plant nearby. Airy, weightless, nobody present. The main subject must sit in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame, leaving a clean, uncluttered, darker LOWER ~40% for text. CRITICAL: any darker area must be darker ONLY because the scene's own light falls off naturally — NOT because a dark band, gradient, vignette or overlay has been applied. There must be NO horizontal boundary, step, line or abrupt change of tone anywhere in the frame; brightness must fall away gradually and continuously. Deliver ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS PHOTOGRAPH natively in 4:5 (1080x1350). Do NOT letterbox, pad, extend or outpaint. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]

slides.title: Prices and dates ((above the fold)).
slides.body: Availability, rate and the book button visible the second the page opens. No scrolling, no hunting, no second click to find out if you're even free.
slides.imagePrompt: A pale stone kitchen island in a bright boutique apartment, a large window behind throwing soft daylight, a ceramic cup and a small plant to one side, warm wood cabinetry in soft focus. Generous open space for UI overlay. NO DEVICE, NO LAPTOP, NO PHONE, NO SCREEN — just the pure scene. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]

slides.title: One reason to book __here__, not there.
slides.body: Parity binds your rate, not your terms. An upgrade, late checkout, breakfast, free cancellation — put one of them on the page and make it loud.
slides.imagePrompt: A soft folded bathrobe and a pair of slippers laid neatly at the corner of a made bed in a boutique hotel room, crisp white linen, warm side light, a sprig of greenery on the tray beside them. Tactile and generous, nobody present. The main subject must sit in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame, leaving a clean, uncluttered, darker LOWER ~40% for text. CRITICAL: any darker area must be darker ONLY because the scene's own light falls off naturally — NOT because a dark band, gradient, vignette or overlay has been applied. There must be NO horizontal boundary, step, line or abrupt change of tone anywhere in the frame; brightness must fall away gradually and continuously. Deliver ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS PHOTOGRAPH natively in 4:5 (1080x1350). Do NOT letterbox, pad, extend or outpaint. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
